create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts when the email matches.
saml.note: Cross-protocol or cross-provider merges by matching email are documented behavior and should not be flagged automatically as identity collapse.

saml.description: SAML application NameID format can be set to Transient, which generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: A changing downstream SAML identifier across sessions is expected when Transient is configured.

saml.description: For third-party applications, API resource scopes and organization scopes that are not enabled for the application are ignored rather than causing an authorization error.
saml.note: A missing granted scope can be expected behavior; do not interpret silent omission as inconsistent authorization binding.

saml.description: For third-party applications, requesting a non-enabled user profile scope results in an error.
saml.note: This differs from API/org scope handling and should be treated as by-design validation behavior.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session and become invalid when the 14-day session expires, regardless of refresh token TTL settings.
saml.note: Expiry in this case is session-driven, not solely token-TTL-driven.

saml.description: When rotate refresh token is enabled, public clients receive a new refresh token on every refresh-token exchange.
saml.note: Refresh token value churn is expected and not evidence of replay detection or token theft mitigation by itself.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Tests that expect JWT claims directly from the access token will fail by design unless a resource or organization is requested.

saml.constraint: Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. For any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have the 'Allow token exchange' setting enabled first, otherwise failures are expected and are not security findings.

For refresh-token lifetime tests, application setting refreshTokenTtlDays does not fully control validity when the original authorization request omitted offline_access. In that case the refresh token is session-bound and the user session has a fixed TTL of 14 days; after session expiry the refresh token becomes invalid regardless of its own TTL. To test refresh-token TTL semantics, the authorization request MUST include scope=offline_access.

Application setting rotateRefreshToken has by-design special behavior: for public clients (SPA and Native), when enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh-token exchange; for other clients, rotation occurs after one year, near expiry (>=70% TTL elapsed), or other documented conditions. Do not treat refresh-token value changes as replay protection failures by themselves.

Application setting refreshTokenTtlDays has protocol-specific availability: it is not available for SPA TTL refreshment, and token requests do not extend TTL for SPA. Tests that assume each refresh extends lifetime MUST NOT use SPA semantics as a freshness oracle.

Redirect URI matching supports wildcard patterns only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and only in hostname/pathname. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. Tests for redirect or flow coherence MUST use exact redirect URIs unless intentionally testing wildcard behavior; wildcard acceptance outside documented positions is invalid setup, not a vulnerability.

Logto does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials and documents direct in-app credential collection as unsupported. Do not build SAML test setup assuming a generic password grant exists for end-user login unless the specific tenant/app exposes such a flow separately. Password-based admin setup should rely on documented admin/operator credentials outside the tested SAML flow.

For token_exchange audience/scope binding tests, the request MUST use the OIDC token endpoint /oidc/token with application/x-www-form-urlencoded body and proper client authentication (Basic auth for confidential clients or client_id in body for public clients). JSON bodies or missing client auth produce setup failures, not security findings.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation and wrong-audience tests, include a control exchange using a valid subject_token and expected resource/scope first. Without a control, token exchange failure may simply indicate the application has not enabled token exchange or client authentication is wrong.

Third-party application permission enforcement is by design restrictive: requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while API resource scopes or organization scopes not enabled for the third-party app are ignored and not granted. I5 tests must distinguish 'error on non-enabled user scope' from 'silently omitted non-enabled API/org scope' to avoid false positives.

Organization scopes are ignored unless the authorization request also includes urn:logto:scope:organizations. For organization-permission tests, the fuzzer MUST request urn:logto:scope:organizations together with organization scopes, otherwise missing organization permissions are expected behavior.

Consent-screen scope display is intersection-based: only scopes already assigned to the user through roles are displayed and grantable to third-party apps. If a requested scope is absent from the user's roles, omission is by design and not an authorization-binding bug. I5 tests must provision user roles containing the target scopes before requesting them.

Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 cross-protocol or SAML email-binding collision tests, account merge by matching email is documented behavior and must not be flagged as an identity-collision vulnerability unless the test specifically proves unauthorized takeover beyond this documented linking rule.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced into primaryEmail, and only verified phone numbers can be synced into primaryPhone. I4 tests that rely on unverified upstream email/phone controlling downstream primary identifiers are invalid unless the upstream attribute is marked verified.

Username matching semantics depend on deployment setting CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME, which defaults to true. Case-based collision tests (e.g., Admin vs admin) MUST account for this deployment setting; differing behavior across deployments may be configuration-driven, not a vulnerability.

For SAML-related testing in Logto, the provided documentation describes Logto acting as a SAML Identity Provider for downstream SAML applications, not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream SAML assertions. Therefore upstream SAML broker attacks such as saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_no_conditions, and saml_wrong_audience are not testable against documented Logto APIs in this protocol run and MUST NOT be inferred from IdP-side docs.

SAML in the provided Logto docs is Logto-as-IdP for SAML applications, not Logto-as-SP consuming upstream SAML assertions. Do NOT attempt to run upstream SAML assertion attacks such as saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_expired_assertion, saml_no_audience_restriction, saml_no_conditions, or saml_wrong_audience against Logto from this documentation set because no SAML ACS / provider-consumption endpoint is documented here.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, the relevant surface is downstream OIDC/OAuth token issuance and userinfo after Logto authenticates the user, not upstream SAML assertion validation. Use OIDC endpoints (/oidc/auth, /oidc/token, /oidc/me, /oidc/token/introspection, /oidc/token/revocation) for verification.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have the 'Allow token exchange' setting enabled, otherwise failures are expected and are not security findings.

Refresh token/session binding: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. Do NOT interpret refresh-token expiry before its configured TTL as an I2 bug unless offline_access was requested; without offline_access, session expiry legitimately invalidates the refresh token.

Application redirect URI matching supports wildcard patterns only in hostname and pathname for SPA and Traditional Web apps. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For flow-coherence tests, do NOT assume exact-match-only redirect URI semantics; wildcard-configured apps may legitimately accept multiple callback hosts/paths within the documented pattern.

Wildcard redirect URIs are explicitly non-standard OIDC and increase attack surface. For security-sensitive I3/I5 tests, prefer exact redirect URIs; otherwise a successful redirect to a wildcard-matched URI may be by design rather than a validation flaw.

Opaque tokens are issued when no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request. JWT-format access tokens are issued when a specific resource or organization is requested. Therefore, verification logic MUST account for token format: use /oidc/me or /oidc/token/introspection for opaque tokens, and do not assume every access token is a JWT.

For I2 token-freshness controls, include a valid control flow alongside any failing attack flow. Logto documentation distinguishes opaque vs JWT issuance based on resource/organization request parameters, so a failed decode or claim check may reflect token format selection rather than freshness enforcement.

Third-party app permission behavior: requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen. I5 tests MUST distinguish 'hard error' from 'silently ignored' based on scope type, or they will misclassify expected behavior as inconsistent authorization.

Organization permissions are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. For I5 organization-scope tests, always include urn:logto:scope:organizations or the absence of organization permissions is by design.

Consent-screen authorization for third-party apps is intersected with user-assigned roles/scopes. If a requested scope is not already assigned to the user through roles, it will be excluded from consent and not granted. I5 escalation tests MUST provision the user with baseline roles first; otherwise missing scopes are expected and not evidence of enforcement at the wrong layer.

Applications of type SPA and Native are public clients and cannot securely store secrets. For token and token-exchange requests from public clients, use client_id in the form body and do NOT require client_secret. For Traditional Web and M2M apps, use client authentication. Misusing client auth mode will cause setup failures unrelated to security invariants.

Rotate refresh token behavior is conditional: a new refresh token is always issued for public clients when enabled, and for other clients when one year has passed since rotation or >=70% of original TTL has elapsed. Do NOT treat refresh-token rotation on every refresh for SPA/Native as anomalous; it is by design.

Refresh token TTL in days is unavailable for SPA in the sense that token requests do not extend TTL. Tests that expect sliding refresh-token lifetime MUST NOT use SPA clients, or expiry behavior will be misinterpreted.

Management API user creation requires at least one identifier among primaryEmail, primaryPhone, or username. Test setup MUST provide one of these; failures without an identifier are expected validation errors, not auth bugs.
Management API PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password is exempt from password policy checks. Do NOT use admin-set passwords to test password-policy enforcement; such bypass is documented behavior.

Custom user customData updates overwrite the original content rather than merge. Tests that patch customData MUST send the full intended final object, or apparent data loss/collision is by design and not an I4 issue.

Only verified email/phone values from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced into primaryEmail/primaryPhone. Cross-protocol or SSO-linking tests that expect unverified upstream identifiers to populate primary fields will produce false positives.

Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving enterprise SSO and local/social identities, same-email account merging is documented behavior and must not be flagged as an identity-collision bug by itself.

NameID format for SAML applications can be Persistent, Email address, Transient, or Unspecified, with default Persistent using the Logto user ID. Any downstream SP-observed identifier changes across sessions under Transient format are by design; do not treat them as principal-binding failures in Logto.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. For any token_exchange test, update_application MUST enable the application's token exchange setting first; otherwise failures are expected and do not indicate an authorization-binding issue.

Refresh token TTL has a sentinel-like upper bound from session binding: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session and becomes invalid after the fixed 14-day session TTL regardless of the configured refresh token TTL. To test refresh-token lifetime semantics correctly, the fuzzer MUST request offline_access when it needs the configured refresh token TTL to take full effect.

Rotate refresh token is effectively mandatory for public clients in practice: when enabled, public clients receive a new refresh token on every refresh. Tests that replay old refresh tokens or assume stable refresh-token values MUST account for rotation, especially for SPA/native-style clients.

Wildcard redirect URIs are supported only for application redirect URI configuration, not as general auth constraint matching. They are non-standard OIDC and increase attack surface. Tests must not treat wildcard redirect support as evidence of weak audience or issuer validation elsewhere.

For I5 token-exchange tests, third-party app permissions are allowlisted per application. Non-enabled user profile scopes cause authorization errors, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'request rejected' from 'scope silently omitted' based on scope type when evaluating over-granting.

User profile scope matching is exact by scope name only; there is no wildcard or pattern mode for scopes. For multi-scope or escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST request explicit scope names and compare granted scopes exactly. Do not use '*' or pattern-like values expecting broad matches.

For I3 config-change tests involving signing keys, Logto documents that consecutive signing-key rotations can invalidate all issued tokens. A valid coherence test must perform at most one rotation between baseline and attack steps; multiple rapid rotations create by-design invalidation and are not evidence of stale trust handling.

Logto's documented SAML support in this corpus is Logto acting as IdP for SAML applications, not Logto consuming upstream SAML assertions as an SP/broker. Therefore SAML ACS-style saml_login, SAML provider creation, and upstream SAML signature/issuer/audience validation operations are not documented here and MUST NOT be invented for this profile run.

Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 collision tests involving SAML/enterprise SSO-style identities, same-email account merging is by design and MUST NOT be flagged as an identity-collision bug unless the test demonstrates unauthorized merge across differing email ownership expectations.

Username case sensitivity is configurable at the deployment level via CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME, while user-data docs describe usernames as case-sensitive. I4 case-confusion tests MUST record the deployment setting before asserting collisions or separations for username-based identities.

For I2 token-freshness controls, opaque access tokens are issued when no resource is specified, while JWT access tokens are issued when a specific resource or organization is requested. The fuzzer MUST keep token format constant between control and attack cases or introspection/userinfo behavior differences may be misread as freshness bugs.

Management API PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password is exempt from password policy checks. Tests that use admin password reset as a setup step MUST NOT infer password-policy enforcement behavior from that endpoint.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
